description: Capacity-planning / sizing view for a Grafana Mimir microservices deployment. Compares required vs requested vs used CPU, memory and disk per component, using the ratios from the Mimir 'Planning capacity' docs.

options.content:
These diagrams show the [architecture of Mimir read / write components](https://grafana.com/docs/mimir/latest/get-started/about-grafana-mimir-architecture/#grafana-mimir-architecture) and the [Ruler architecture](https://grafana.com/docs/mimir/latest/references/architecture/components/ruler/) \
The highest % CPU, Memory, Storage result is displayed on the charts

graph LR
subgraph Mimir Write Path Services Highest % Used
A{{Writes}} --> 1.1([Distributor])
1.1([Distributor])--> 1.2([Ingester])
1.2([Ingester]) --> 1.3[(ObjectStorage)]
1.4([Compactor]) --> 1.3[(ObjectStorage)]
end

targets.expr:
((sum by (cluster) (kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", job="kubelet", namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolumeclaim=~".*ingester.*"}))
- 
(sum by (cluster) (kubelet_volume_stats_available_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", job="kubelet", namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolumeclaim=~".*ingester.*"})))
/
(sum by (cluster)(kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", job="kubelet", namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolumeclaim=~".*ingester.*"}))
* 100

options.content:
To work out sizing on these panels, the following calculations are used from this article: [Distributor: Mimir Capacity Doc](https://grafana.com/docs/mimir/latest/operators-guide/run-production-environment/planning-capacity/#distributor)
* CPU: 1 core every 25,000 samples per second.
* Memory: 1GB every 25,000 samples per second. 

The panels to the right represent per replica current sizing and usage. \
The below panels represent estimated cluster wide scale based on current ingestion. They show growth trends over timeshift period, defined in a dashboard variable.

To work out sizing on these panels, the following calculations are used from this article: [Ingester: Mimir Capacity Doc](https://grafana.com/docs/mimir/latest/operators-guide/run-production-environment/planning-capacity/#ingester)
* CPU: 1 core for every 300,000 series in memory
* Memory: 2.5GB for every 300,000 series in memory
* Disk space: 5GB for every 300,000 series in memory

The panels to the right represent per replica current sizing and usage. \
The below panels represent estimated cluster wide scale based on current ingestion. They show growth trends over timeshift period, defined in a dashboard variable.

targets.expr: sum without(instance, node) (topk(1, kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolumeclaim=~".*ingester.*", job="kubelet"}))

sum without(instance, node) (kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", job="kubelet", namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolumeclaim=~".*ingester.*"}) - topk(100, sum without(instance, node) (kubelet_volume_stats_available_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", job="kubelet", namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolumeclaim=~".*ingester.*"}))

sum by(cluster) (kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", job="kubelet", namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolumeclaim=~".*ingester.*"}) - topk(100, sum by(cluster) (kubelet_volume_stats_available_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", job="kubelet", namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolumeclaim=~".*ingester.*"}))

sum by(cluster) (kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", job="kubelet", namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolumeclaim=~".*ingester.*"}) - topk(100, sum by(cluster) (kubelet_volume_stats_available_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", job="kubelet", namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolumeclaim=~".*ingester.*"}))

To work out sizing on these panels, the following calculations are used from this article: [Query-frontend: Mimir Capacity Doc](https://grafana.com/docs/mimir/latest/operators-guide/run-production-environment/planning-capacity/#query-frontend)
* CPU: 1 core for every 250 queries per second
* Memory: 1GB for every 250 queries per second

The panels to the right represent per replica current sizing and usage. \
The below panels represent estimated cluster wide scale based on current query usage. They show growth trends over timeshift period, defined in a dashboard variable.

To work out sizing on these panels, the following calculations are used from this article: [Alertmanager: Mimir Capacity Doc](https://grafana.com/docs/mimir/latest/operators-guide/run-production-environment/planning-capacity/#optional-alertmanager)
* CPU: 1 core for every 100 firing alert notifications per second
* Memory: 1GB for every 5,000 firing alerts

The panels to the right represent per replica current sizing and usage. \
The below panels represent estimated cluster wide scale based on current query usage. They show growth trends over timeshift period, defined in a dashboard variable.

The advice on these panels is from this article: [Caches: Mimir Capacity Doc](https://grafana.com/docs/mimir/latest/operators-guide/run-production-environment/planning-capacity/#optional-caches)

A rule of thumb for scaling memcached deployments for these caches is to look at the rate of evictions. \
If it `0` during steady load and only with occasional spikes, then memcached is sufficiently scaled. \
If it is `>0` all the time, then memcached needs to be scaled out.
